title: Minify the channel to one atomic layer: MoS2 vertical access
idea: Shrink the access-transistor body to a 0.65 nm MoS2/WSe2 monolayer wrapped gate-all-around on the pillar sidewall; with no bulk volume and no doped junctions, subthreshold and junction-generation leakage both collapse. Semimetal Bi/Sb contacts keep on-current above ~20 uA.
why: Leakage tail (<=13 fA) targeted below 0.1 fA; retention 64 ms -> ~10 s, cutting refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit) and the 10-20% refresh bandwidth loss by >90%.

title: Magnify the gate-drain underlap to defuse GIDL
idea: Stretch a 15-25 nm ungated, lightly doped drain extension along the vertical pillar between wordline and storage node so peak drain field drops from ~1.5 to <0.6 MV/cm, exponentially suppressing band-to-band (GIDL) and trap-assisted tunneling. A thin fringing field plate tied to the bitline restores on-current.
why: GIDL/TAT dominate the retention tail; 10-100x lower tail current lifts minimum retention and stretches the refresh interval 4-8x.

title: Minify temperature to 77 K for pooled rack memory
idea: Put CXL-attached memory pools in a liquid-nitrogen dewar shelf: at 77 K subthreshold and generation leakage fall ~10^6x so retention reaches hours and refresh essentially stops, while lower wire resistance lets VARY drop to ~0.6 V. One cryocooler serves terabytes shared by a whole rack.
why: Removes refresh's 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth tax; CV^2 energy ~2.5x lower; cryo overhead amortized across the pool.

title: Weak-cell exile: banish leakage-tail cells to a tiny SRAM
idea: Profile per-cell retention at test and periodically in the field, remap the ~0.01-0.1% of cells with retention <1 s into an on-die SRAM/CAM patch table keyed by address, and refresh the remaining 99.9% at 1 s instead of 64 ms. Online re-profiling catches variable-retention-time cells.
why: Minifying who sets the refresh rate magnifies the interval ~16x: refresh energy and bandwidth tax down ~16x for <0.5% die area.

title: Magnify the threshold during storage with a pulsed back-plate
idea: Give vertical-channel access transistors a buried back-gate plate per subarray held at -1.5 V during retention (raising Vt ~0.4 V by body effect) and pulsed to 0 V only in the subarray being activated. Leakage falls ~10^4x in storage while access on-current is untouched.
why: Breaks the leakage-vs-speed trade-off behind refresh (fact 3); refresh interval 10-50x longer.

title: Magnify off-resistance to a vacuum gap: NEMS access relay
idea: Replace the access transistor with a 30 nm torsional nanoelectromechanical contact relay (Ru/RuO2 tip, 3-5 nm sealed vacuum gap) pulled in by the wordline; when open the gap passes essentially zero current, leaving only capacitor dielectric leakage. Hermetic BEOL sealing targets 1e15 contact cycles.
why: Deletes the access-device leakage tail entirely; retention limited by the dielectric (minutes-hours), refresh nearly eliminated; contact endurance is the risk.

title: Magnify abruptness: NbO2 threshold switch in series (Hyper-FET)
idea: Insert a 10 nm NbO2 Mott threshold-switching layer between access transistor and storage node: below ~0.4 V it is insulating, cutting off-current 100-1000x, and when the wordline drives the cell above threshold it snaps metallic within ns. Its hysteresis window is tuned so stored '1' levels sit in the insulating regime.
why: Effective subthreshold swing <10 mV/dec cuts the leakage tail 100x+ without raising Vt; refresh ~10x rarer.

title: Minify the swing with a band-to-band tunneling access FET
idea: Make the access device a vertical heterojunction TFET (SiGe source at the bitline, Si channel, drain into storage node) whose off-state has no thermionic Boltzmann tail, so off-current is set by tunneling (~1e-18 A). Its low on-current is offset by short local bitlines.
why: Off-current decoupled from kT: refresh interval ~10x longer, and wordline swing can fall from ~3 V to ~1.5 V (fact 10).

title: Magnify refresh duration, minify energy: adiabatic resonant refresh
idea: Refresh whole banks slowly with microsecond ramps driven by an on-package LC resonator that swings wordlines and bitline precharge sinusoidally and recovers charge each cycle, so dissipation scales as (RC/T)*CV^2 instead of CV^2. Refresh has no latency requirement, so stretching it costs nothing.
why: Refresh energy ~46 fJ/bit -> ~5-10 fJ/bit (5-10x lower).

title: Minify bitlines for refresh: 16-cell local sense nodes
idea: Add a hierarchical micro-sense amplifier every 16 cells (placed under the array via bonded CMOS) used only for refresh, so each cell restores against a ~1 fF local bitline rather than a 50-100 fF global one. Normal reads still use the global path.
why: Bitline charge per refreshed bit drops >10x; all subarrays can refresh in parallel, hiding the 10-20% bandwidth loss.

title: Magnify leakage on purpose: canary cells set refresh pace
idea: Seed every subarray with replica canary cells built 5-10x leakier (shorter channel, deliberate defect implant) that are sensed cheaply on a slow timer; a subarray is refreshed only when its canaries decay. Refresh then tracks real temperature, voltage and aging instead of a worst-case 85 C spec.
why: Real leakage is usually 10-50x below worst case, so refresh energy and bandwidth drop ~10x on average.

title: Magnify ECC to a full 8 KB row LDPC merged with refresh
idea: Store ~3% row-length LDPC parity inside each row and stretch refresh to 1-2 s; every refresh activation decodes on-die and writes back corrected bits, so refresh doubles as scrubbing and retention-tail errors never accumulate.
why: Refresh interval 16-32x longer: refresh bandwidth and energy down >90% for ~3% area.

title: Minify charged cells: discharge-biased coding skips empty-row refresh
idea: The controller encodes each line (XOR with a learned base plus bus-invert, polarity flipped for true/anti-cell subarrays) so >90% of cells sit in the discharged, non-leaking state, and a per-row flag marks rows with no charged cells, which are never refreshed.
why: Only charged cells need refresh; zero-heavy and sparse tensor data yields 2-5x fewer refreshed rows.

title: Magnify isolation: storage node floats on buried oxide, no junction
idea: Form the storage-node contact region on a local buried-oxide pocket created by Si/SiGe selective etch-and-fill, so the storage node touches no p-n junction or substrate and the only leakage paths left are the gated channel and the capacitor.
why: Junction generation and trap-assisted tunneling are a large share of the tail; removing them targets ~10x longer minimum retention.

title: Magnify the gate count: two series wordlines per vertical pillar
idea: Stack two independently driven gate-all-around segments along each vertical access pillar; both turn on for access, but in standby the intermediate node self-biases to give the upper device negative Vgs (stack effect), dropping subthreshold leakage 10-30x.
why: Leakage tail down 10-30x at 4F^2 using only extra height; refresh interval ~8x.

title: Minify dark carriers: light-gated photoconductive access switches
idea: Use a wide-bandgap photoconductor strip (amorphous GaN or ZnS, dark resistivity >1e14 ohm-cm) as each access switch, turned on by an on-chip waveguide routing 365 nm light to the selected row through micro-ring selectors; in the dark it is an insulator and there is no wordline to charge.
why: Leakage ~0 in the dark; eliminates 3 V wordline CV^2 (fact 10); refresh far rarer; switching speed and optical power budget are the risks.

title: Minify refresh to zero: tunnel-diode trickle latch per cell
idea: Stack a pair of nanoscale Esaki interband-tunnel diodes (Goto pair) on the capacitor top electrode; their N-shaped I-V creates two stable node voltages that continuously replace leaked charge with ~10 fA standby current, so the cell holds itself like SRAM at near-DRAM size.
why: Refresh eliminated; standby stays <2 mW for 16 Gb if diode valley currents are tuned to 10-100 fA.

title: Magnify cells per bit on demand: OS-elastic twin-cell mode
idea: Let the OS/hypervisor flip under-used DRAM regions into 2-cells-per-bit differential mode (complementary cells on paired bitlines) that tolerates ~10x more charge loss and is refreshed at 1 s; regions revert to 1 cell/bit when demand rises, controlled by a per-subarray mode register.
why: Trades idle capacity for refresh: idle rack memory refresh power down ~10x with no process change.

title: Minify the refreshed footprint: compress-then-park unrefreshed rows
idea: The memory controller compresses cold pages (base-delta/LZ, ~2-3x) into packed regions and disables refresh on the vacated rows using subarray-granular partial-array self-refresh, so the refreshed footprint shrinks with the data.
why: Refresh energy scales with refreshed rows: 2-3x lower idle refresh power, plus freed capacity.

title: Magnify the retention tail into a product: long-retention premium bin
idea: Measure each die's retention distribution at wafer sort and sell the top-quartile dies as 'LR' parts with a guaranteed 256 ms-1 s refresh spec at a premium to hyperscalers; controllers read the bin and lengthen tREFI accordingly.
why: Monetizes existing variation: 4-16x less refresh on LR parts, more effective bandwidth and lower power without new fabs.

title: Minify one-size refresh: JEDEC per-module retention negotiation field
idea: Push a JEDEC addition where each module publishes a measured, temperature-indexed retention table in SPD, re-measured by in-field self-test, and the controller negotiates tREFI from it instead of the fixed 64/32 ms rule.
why: Industry-wide 2-8x refresh reduction on most parts at zero silicon cost.

title: Minify trap density: millisecond laser anneal of storage junction
idea: After the storage-node implant, apply a sub-millisecond laser/flash anneal that heals end-of-range implant defects without diffusing dopants, then high-pressure deuterium sintering to passivate remaining mid-gap traps that create trap-assisted tunneling and variable retention time.
why: Shrinks the <=13 fA tail population ~10x; minimum retention up 2-4x.

title: Magnify restore voltage only on refresh: overdrive write-back
idea: During refresh (not normal access) sense amps restore '1' cells to ~1.4 V from a separate boosted restore rail with a brief overdriven wordline, storing ~40% more charge so cells take longer to decay to the sense threshold; normal accesses keep the low VARY.
why: Retention ~1.5-2x longer so refresh frequency halves; net refresh energy ~30-40% lower; dielectric reliability is the watch item.

title: Magnify bandgap to 3.3 eV: SiC-junction DRAM holding charge for decades
idea: Build the storage junction and access transistor in 4H-SiC, whose intrinsic carrier density (~1e-9 cm^-3 vs 1e10 for Si) cuts thermal generation current by ~18 orders of magnitude, so a charged node holds >10 years at 85 C with the access device off. The read/write scheme stays DRAM-like and U.S. SiC power-device lines can host it.
why: Data survives power loss and refresh disappears (fact 3); reuses domestic SiC fabs; MOS interface traps and density are the risks.

title: Magnify mechanical inertia: bistable buckled nanobeam bit
idea: Store each bit as the up/down state of a pre-compressed, snap-through-bistable 100 nm SiN nanobeam; electrodes above and below snap it in ns and its position is read capacitively by a gain transistor. No charge is retained, so nothing leaks, and elastic flexing has no oxide-breakdown wear mechanism.
why: Non-volatile, zero refresh, abundant materials; elastic endurance targeted >1e15.

title: Minify displacement to sub-angstrom: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer access gate
idea: Use bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 whose ~0.1 nm interlayer stacking slide flips out-of-plane polarization as the gate stack of a 2D-channel transistor, setting Vt non-volatilely. Switching is interlayer sliding with no ion motion or bond breaking, so there is no wake-up, fatigue or imprint mechanism.
why: Non-volatile 1T cell with potentially unlimited endurance, sub-1 V write, no capacitor and no refresh.

title: Magnify endurance with antiferroelectric ZrO2 given a built-in bias
idea: Antiferroelectric ZrO2 survives 1e12+ cycles but has no remanence; asymmetric electrodes (TiN vs RuO2 work-function offset) plus a fixed-charge dipole interlayer shift the double loop so one AFE loop straddles zero field, creating two stable remanent states.
why: Non-volatile cells with endurance 100-1000x beyond HZO FeRAM; refresh-free.

title: Magnify the dielectric's job: linear high-k by day, ferroelectric at shutdown
idea: Make the DRAM capacitor dielectric a ZrO2/HfZrO2 morphotropic blend that acts as a k~50 linear dielectric under normal +/-0.5 V operation, and only when a power-loss detector fires a 2.5 V plate pulse is stored charge converted into remanent polarization; a power-up pulse converts it back.
why: DRAM-class endurance during operation plus survival of power loss; ferroelectric fatigue spent only once per power cycle; higher k also helps Cs (fact 1).

title: Magnify Vt shift to latch the access device permanently off
idea: Insert a thin HZO ferroelectric in each access-transistor gate stack; on power loss one global wordline pulse flips every access gate into a +1.2 V Vt-shifted deep-off state, trapping capacitor charge behind <1e-21 A leakage until power returns and a reset pulse restores normal Vt.
why: Turns conventional 1T1C into a power-loss-surviving memory with one FE switch per power cycle; also reduces refresh in operation.

title: Magnify barrier opacity: electron Bragg-mirror superlattice floating node
idea: Surround a charge-storage node with a Si/SiO2 (or ZnO/MgZnO) superlattice engineered so thermal electrons fall in a miniband gap and are reflected, while a ~2 V bias aligns a resonant miniband for ns-scale transport; zero-bias leakage is blocked without Fowler-Nordheim stress.
why: Flash-like retention with DRAM-like 10 ns writes and low oxide damage (endurance >>1e12 targeted); refresh-free.

title: Minify oxide damage: write floating gates with photons, not fields
idea: Program floating-gate cells by internal photoemission: an on-chip waveguide delivers ~3.5 eV photons that lift electrons over a thick 8 nm SiO2 barrier at low field, so the oxide never sees the high-field stress that limits flash to ~1e5 cycles; hole photoemission erases. The thick oxide gives 10-year retention.
why: Non-volatile, refresh-free, potentially 1e12+ endurance; write speed set by optical power per row with full-row parallel writes.

title: Minify refresh to nanowatts and feed it with a betavoltaic cell
idea: Pair hour-retention cells with a sleep-mode refresh interval of ~1 h and integrate a Ni-63 or tritium betavoltaic film on the package supplying microwatts for decades, so the module keeps its data alive after mains loss with no battery to wear out.
why: A 16 Gb die refreshed hourly needs ~0.2 uW (46 fJ/bit); volatile cells become effectively non-volatile with zero grid idle power.

title: Minify the flush: dirty-line tracking plus deep-trench energy bank
idea: Each DRAM bank tracks dirty rows in a bitmap and keeps an on-die deep-trench capacitor bank sized only to flush the dirty fraction into a co-integrated MRAM shadow subarray at power loss; clean rows are already mirrored in NV storage.
why: Persistence with no supercaps or batteries: hold-up energy 10-100x smaller; DRAM speed and endurance kept, NV wear only from dirty data.

title: Magnify the log, minify the NV tier: per-store persistent journal
idea: Mirror every store into a 64 MB MRAM ring-buffer journal on the module (64 B appends via write combining) with periodic incremental snapshots to NAND; after power loss full DRAM state is rebuilt by snapshot plus journal replay.
why: Whole-DRAM persistence for ~0.5% added NV capacity with no change to the DRAM cell; the ring wear-levels itself.

title: Minify the access device to nothing: self-rectifying ferroelectric diode crossbar
idea: Use Sc-doped AlN or BiFeO3 ferroelectric layers whose polarization flips the Schottky barrier at one electrode, producing a diode whose forward direction encodes the bit; the cell rectifies itself, so a passive crossbar needs no transistor and stacks in many BEOL layers with non-destructive current read.
why: Removes the access transistor and its leakage; 4F^2 per layer times stacking; non-volatile; avoids destructive read (fact 8).

title: Minify the switch to two terminals: OTS selector plus FE capacitor
idea: Pair each ferroelectric capacitor with an ovonic threshold switch selector in a 1S1C stack: half-select voltages stay below the OTS threshold so unselected cells see no disturb, while the selected cell gets the full switching pulse; 4-8 layers stack above CMOS periphery.
why: Eliminates planar access transistor area and epitaxial silicon per layer; non-volatile 3D density multiplication.

title: Minify transistors per bit: VCMA-gated spin-orbit strip with 8 MTJs
idea: Place 8 MTJs on one tungsten-free (Pt-alloy or BiSb) spin-orbit-torque write strip with a single access transistor; a voltage on each MTJ's top electrode lowers its anisotropy (VCMA) so only that MTJ flips when strip current passes, and reads use the same per-MTJ electrode.
why: One transistor per 8 bits, non-volatile, unlimited MTJ endurance, ns writes; ~3x SOT-MRAM density; sidesteps the tungsten chokepoint.

title: Magnify the domain wall into the switch: LiNbO3 conductive-wall cells
idea: In thin-film LiNbO3 nanofins a write pulse nucleates or erases a charged domain wall across the fin; the wall conducts ~1e6x better than bulk, so the cell reads on/off non-destructively and has no leakage path when the wall is absent. Walls are stable indefinitely at room temperature.
why: Non-volatile, non-destructive read (fact 8), no stored charge to leak; LiNbO3 thin films already run in photonics fabs.

title: Minify the switching volume: hidden-state Mott charge-density-wave bits
idea: Exploit the metastable 'hidden' metallic state of 1T-TaS2 (strain-engineered to stay stable above room temperature): a 10 ns current pulse switches a nanoflake between insulating CDW and metastable metallic order with 10-100x resistance contrast that persists unpowered.
why: Electronic rather than ionic switching promises unlimited endurance and sub-pJ writes; room-temperature stability is the open question.

title: Minify the charge to a few electrons on Coulomb-blockaded nanodots
idea: Store bits as 5-10 electrons on sub-3 nm Si nanodots whose charging energy (>10 kT) blocks thermally activated escape, sensed non-destructively by a gate-coupled single-electron transistor; writes use direct tunneling through ~2 nm oxide at low voltage, avoiding high-field wear.
why: Non-volatile via quantized charging energy, fJ writes, extreme density; room-temperature uniformity is the risk.

title: Minify write voltage to 100 mV: magnetoelectric BiFeO3-gated nanomagnets
idea: Couple a multiferroic BiFeO3 layer to a CoFe nanomagnet so a ~100 mV field reverses BFO polarization and, via exchange coupling, flips the magnet; an MTJ stacked on top reads it. Write current is capacitive only, so the access transistor can be minimum-width.
why: Non-volatile, aJ-class write, escapes the CV^2 voltage floor (fact 10); FE endurance in BFO is the limit.

title: Minify grain to one domain: wall-free ferroelectric nanodots for fatigue immunity
idea: Pattern HZO into <=8 nm epitaxial single-domain islands on a templated seed so each switches coherently without domain-wall nucleation or pinning, removing the defect-redistribution paths behind wake-up and fatigue; arrays of dots form each cell capacitor.
why: Targets FeRAM endurance from ~1e11 to >1e15 for a non-volatile DRAM replacement; tighter switching distribution also lowers voltage.

title: Magnify the barrier to vacuum: field-emission-written floating islands
idea: Suspend a metal storage island in a sealed 5 nm vacuum nanocavity, write it by field emission from a sharpened tip electrode (1-2 V across nm gaps), and read it by capacitive coupling to a gain FET. Vacuum has no traps to wear out and essentially no zero-bias conduction.
why: Non-volatile, refresh-free, endurance not limited by oxide damage; uses common metals (Mo, Ti).

title: Magnify the value of persistence: kill AI checkpoint memory overhead
idea: Sell non-volatile DRAM-class modules to AI training clusters as checkpoint-free memory: training state persists through power events in place, eliminating host-DRAM staging buffers and periodic checkpoint copies.
why: Recovers ~10-20% of cluster memory capacity and step time; creates a premium launch market that funds NV-DRAM lines.

title: Magnify demand signal: federal persistent-memory procurement on legacy U.S. fabs
idea: A CHIPS-style advance market commitment obliges federal datacenters to buy a quota of U.S.-made non-volatile working memory (SiC, AFE, LiNbO3 or MRAM flavors) built on 28-90 nm domestic legacy lines that need no EUV.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital intensity: legacy-line conversions ~$1-2B vs $15B+ for a new DRAM fab; seeds domestic supply.

title: Minify idle power to zero: park non-volatile memory ranks fully off
idea: Because NV working memory keeps data unpowered, the hypervisor consolidates hot pages and cuts power entirely (not just refresh) to idle ranks within microseconds, so a power-capped rack can install ~2x more memory at the same watts.
why: Removes refresh and standby power completely and converts power-limited deployments into more usable memory.
